pi.name: Ping He
pi.title: Professor of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology
pi.bio: Ping He is a Professor in the Department of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology at the University of Michigan. He received his B.S. from China Agricultural University, his M.S. from the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and his Ph.D. from Kansas State University, followed by postdoctoral training at Harvard Medical School. His research focuses on the activation and signaling mechanisms of host immunity upon pathogen infection, using Arabidopsis as a model, and on how signaling crosstalk orchestrates plant responses to extrinsic and intrinsic signals, with applications toward improving crop resilience. He co-leads the Molecular Plant-Microbe Interaction laboratory with Professor Libo Shan.

description: The He lab is part of the Molecular Plant-Microbe Interaction (MPMI) laboratory at the University of Michigan, a shared research group co-led by Ping He and Libo Shan. The group studies how plants recognize microbes and activate immune signaling, focusing on the activation and attenuation of pattern recognition receptor (PRR) complexes and NLR immune receptors. Research spans transcriptional, post-transcriptional, and post-translational regulation of plant immunity, including alternative splicing and protein kinase signaling; the coordination of immunity with growth and development; the regulation of plant autoimmunity; and immunomodulatory phytocytokines. Arabidopsis is the primary model, with translational work in cotton disease resistance and abiotic stress adaptation.

areas.title: Activation and attenuation of plant PRR complexes and signaling
areas.summary: Examines how plants activate and regulate pattern recognition receptor signaling pathways in response to microbial threats.

areas.title: Transcriptional, post-transcriptional, and post-translational regulation of plant immunity
areas.summary: Investigates multiple levels of gene expression control, including alternative splicing and phosphorylation, that govern plant defense against pathogens.

areas.title: Coordination of plant immunity, growth, and development
areas.summary: Studies how plants balance immune responses with growth and developmental processes under environmental stress.

areas.title: Regulation of plant autoimmunity
areas.summary: Explores mechanisms, including E3 ligases, chaperones, and calcium signaling, that prevent plants from mounting excessive self-damaging immune reactions.

areas.title: Immunomodulatory phytocytokines in plant immunity
areas.summary: Analyzes peptide signaling molecules that coordinate and fine-tune plant immune activation.

areas.title: Cotton disease resistance and abiotic stress adaptation
areas.summary: Applies functional and translational genomics to identify disease-resistant traits and improve stress resilience in cotton.
